evidence.note: Tracks per-crate status ('rusternetes-common now compiles its tests; next leaf crate is storage'), showing a per-crate green/stuck picture — but this is compile status, not test-pass status.

Uses compile-error counts ('87 errors', '68 total errors', '154 errors') as a rough progress proxy. This is the closest it comes to a tally, but it tracks compile errors, never test passes against the 1,390-test horizon.

Notices self-inflicted regressions (duplicate DaemonSet aliases, duplicate current_replicas/unavailable_replicas fields, removing 'extra' from wrong UserInfo) and corrects them — genuine local regression awareness.
Repeatedly loops on the shared WorkloadSpec/WorkloadStatus type toggling Option vs direct fields across ~30+ steps — circular debugging that it does not flag as a loop while it is happening.

Only very late (step 180 of 188) names the stuck/circular state ('This approach is not converging'; 'has not converged... would require a full redesign'), and re-verifies common still compiles — late detection rather than an active monitor. Never runs any tests, so it has no accounting of how much of the suite is actually green.

reasoning: The agent maintains per-crate compile status and uses error counts as a crude progress proxy, and it catches regressions it introduces (above the level-3 'doesn't notice regressions/repeated failures' anchor). But it never runs a single test, so it has no picture of 'how much of the suite is green' across the 1,390-test / 100-binary horizon — the core of this dimension — and it detects its own circular debugging on WorkloadSpec/status only in the final ~5% of the run after dozens of thrashing iterations. That places it just below the level-5 anchor (which requires noticing a stuck crate and a rough sense of suite greenness) and well short of level-8's concrete pass-count ledger, landing at 4.
